 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 07-07-2022 at about 9.45 a.m., the petitioner was riding the Star City motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-AD-5532, along with his father as a pillion rider, on the extreme left side on Magadi main road, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations.

While so proceeding, when he reached opposite to Samruddi Hotel,
near Ganesha Temple, Sunkadakatte, Bengaluru City, all of sudden the driver of the Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982, came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sri Lakshmi Multi-Speciality Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Spine Care and Ortho Care Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Earlier to the accident, he was working as artist and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.

But, due to the accidental injuries,
he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Kamakshipalya Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Mahendra Maxima Goods vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.

4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained,
medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

It has contended that, the alleged accident has taken place due to the self negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-KK-5532, who was riding his motorcycle along with pillion rider in negligent manner and high speed, unmindful of the traffic, resulting in the accident.
The petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
It has denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No. KA- 02-AD-0982.

It has contended that, its liability if any is subject to the driver of the vehicle having proper, valid and effective driving licence, permit and fitness to drive the vehicle allegedly involved in the accident.
Further, it sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 07-07-2022 at about 9.45 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Mahendra Maxima Goods Vehicle,
bearing registration No. KA-02-AD-0982 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. S.S.
Amarnath as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.
7. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 07-07-2022 at about 9.45 a.m., when he was riding the Star City motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-AD-5532, along with his father as a pillion rider, on the extreme left side on Magadi main road, opposite to Samruddi Hotel, near Ganesha Temple, Sunkadakatte, Bengaluru City, slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations, all of sudden the driver of offending Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982, came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motorcycle from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as artist and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
10. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of sketch,
Ex.P.5 is certified copy of notice under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicels Act and reply to said notice, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of wound certificate,
Ex.P.8 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.9 is discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is estimation for removal of implant, Ex.P.11 is notarised copy of Aadhar card, Ex.P.12 is notarised copy of ID card,
Ex.P.13 are medical bills (total 5), Ex.P.14 are prescriptions (total 3), Ex.P.15 is x-ray, Ex.P.16 is case sheet, Ex.P.17 is medical certificate and Ex.P.18 are x-rays (total 3).

11. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 8, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982 and dashing the same to the ongoing motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-AD-5532 of the petitioner.

Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries to his right leg i.e. puncture wound over the anteromedial aspect of right lower leg, deformity in the right leg, displaced fractures of tibia and fibula at the lower 3rd of his right leg.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.8,
has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA- 02-AD-0982.
12.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982 in the accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 with respect to said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company, though has specifically denied the above stated facts in its written statement and taken specific defence that, the said accident is caused due to self rash and negligent driving on the part of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Ganesh.M vs Harsha G.K on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85873854/
4 No.KA-02-KK-5532 and not wearing helmet at the time of accident, has failed to establish the said contentions.

The respondent No.2 has neither adduced any evidence to establish the said contentions, nor it has produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Even, the respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in its written statement on oath.

On the other hand, the petitioner/P.W.1, has unequivocally denied the suggestions made in his cross- examination that, the accident in question is caused due to his self rash and negligent driving and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of on Magadi main road, opposite to Samruddi Hotel, near Ganesha Temple, Sunkadakatte, Bengaluru City, due to dashing of offending Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982 to the ongoing motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-AD-5532 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.8 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Mahindra Maxima goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD- 0982.
Admittedly, the Ex.P.8 final report/chare-sheet filed by the investigation officer has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 14.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.9 discharge summary,
Ex.P.15 x-ray, Ex.P.16 case sheet, Ex.P.17 medical certificate and Ex.P.18 x- rays, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered puncture wound over the anteromedial aspect of right lower leg, deformity in the right leg, displaced fractures of tibia and fibula at the lower 3 rd of his right leg.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.2, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the Ganesh.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

17. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 07-07-2022 at about 9:45 a.m., on Magadi main road, opposite to Samruddi Hotel, near Ganesha Temple, Sunkadakatte,
Bengaluru City, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, the petitioner has sustained puncture wound over the anteromedial aspect of right lower leg, deformity in the right leg, displaced fractures of tibia and fibula at the lower 3rd of his right leg and for the said injuries he has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning,
future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.11.
As per Ex.P.11, the date of birth of the petitioner is 30-06-1986.
The accident has taken place on 07-07-2022 at about 9:45 a.m.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 36 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has sustained Ganesh.M vs Harsha G.K on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85873854/
6 puncture wound over the anteromedial aspect of right lower leg, deformity in the right leg, displaced fractures of tibia and fibula at the lower 3 rd of his right leg.
Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 11% physical disability to the whole body.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.

The Ex.P.7 wound certificate,
Ex.P.9 discharge summary, Ex.P.15 x-ray, Ex.P.16 case sheet, Ex.P.17 medical certificate and Ex.P.18 x-rays clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained puncture wound over the anteromedial aspect of right lower leg, deformity in the right leg, displaced fractures of tibia and fibula at the lower 3rd of his right leg.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth
has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to his cross- examination that,
there is no disability to the petitioner and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 07-07-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 22-02-2024,
which is after lapse of one year and seven months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of entire treatment.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture sustained by the petitioner are united with implants in situ.

Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner,
duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.

Hence,
in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as artist and was earning a sum of Rs.50,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
To substantiate the same he has produced notarised copy of ID card as per Ex.P.12.
From this document it is clear that, the petitioner was working at Lakshmi Enterprises.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.

Further, the petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, even now he is working in the same company where he was working before the date of accident and he is receiving the same salary.
Therefore, it is clear that the petitioner is continued in the same job and doing the same work as he was doing before the accident and the disability suffered by him has not affecting his work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by him does not arise at all.

For the disability suffered by him,
the petitioner may get compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due to disability.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.

7 ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 5 medical bills, as per Ex.P.13.

But, in the cross-examination the P.W.1 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination, in last 4th line that, the medical expenses incurred for his treatment has been reimbursed by Employees State Insurance.

Therefore, in such circumstances, considering that the entire medical bills have been paid by Employees State Insurance, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.,
puncture wound over the anteromedial aspect of right lower leg, deformity in the right leg, displaced fractures of tibia and fibula at the lower 3rd of his right leg.
As per Ex.P.9 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 6 days from 07-07-2022 to 12-07-2022, in Spine Care and Ortho Care Hospital, Bengaluru.

In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

The petitioner is the resident of Magadi main road, near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Anjananagara, Bengaluru, the accident took place opposite to Samruddi Hotel, near Ganesha Temple, Sunkadakatte, Bengaluru City and he has taken treatment at Spine Care and Ortho Care Hospital, Bengaluru.

vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, now also he is working in the same company as he was working before to the accident and he was receiving the same salary.
Further the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of income during treatment period does not arise at all.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.

8 viii) Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 36 years and unfortunately he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
He has sustained puncture wound over the anteromedial aspect of right lower leg, deformity in the right leg, displaced fractures of tibia and fibula at the lower 3 rd of his right leg.
The evidence shows that, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants and the approximate cost of the said surgery is Rs.50,000/-.
To substantiate the same, she has produced estimation for removal of implant as per Ex.P.10.
The cost of surgery quoted by P.W.2 seems exaggerated.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

19. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. -Nil- 2.
Medical expenses -Nil- 3. Pain and sufferings 40,000-00 4. Attendant charges 6,000-00
5. Food and nourishment 4,800-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 3,000-00 7. Loss of income during -Nil- treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00
9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00

In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,03,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-AD-0982 the said accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained Ganesh.M vs Harsha G.K on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85873854/
9 grievous injuries.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,03,800/-
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,03,800/- (Rupees one lakh three thousand eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
While so proceeding, when he reached opposite to Samruddi Hotel,
near Ganesha Temple, Sunkadakatte, Bengaluru City, all of sudden the driver of the Mahindra Maxima Goods vehicle bearing No.KA-02-AD-0982, came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner from behind and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
opennyai_summary.issue:

bearing registration No. KA-02-AD-0982 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.2 has neither adduced any evidence to establish the said contentions, nor it has produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident 14.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can be safely held that, the respondent No.2 has failed to rebut the Ganesh.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of entire treatment.
If the disability had been assessed after future surgery, perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.
Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture sustained by the petitioner are united with implants in situ.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner,
duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence,
in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
Therefore, it is clear that the petitioner is continued in the same job and doing the same work as he was doing before the accident and the disability suffered by him has not affecting his work.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of future income due to permanent disability suffered by him does not arise at all.
For the disability suffered by him,
the petitioner may get compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort, but not under the head loss of future income due to disability.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.
Therefore, in such circumstances, considering that the entire medical bills have been paid by Employees State Insurance, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of medical expenses.
Further the petitioner has not produced any document to show that, he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for loss of income during treatment period does not arise at all.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this particular head.

9. Future medical expenses 20,000-00
Total Rs. 1,03,800-00
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,03,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,03,800/-
from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,03,800/- (Rupees one lakh three thousand eight hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
